name: lox
algorithm: Compile and run, on the lox dogfood's bytecode VM with its mark-and-sweep collector, the program of its bench script with larger counts: a recursive Fibonacci, a list of strings pushed and dropped every 100, and an arithmetic loop; print the three results (README.md).
args: fun fib(n) { if (n < 2) return n; return fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1); } print fib(26); var xs = []; for (var i = 0; i < 60000; i = i + 1) { push(xs, str(i)); if (len(xs) > 100) xs = []; } print len(xs); var sum = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 600000; i = i + 1) sum = sum + i % 7; print sum;
quick: fun fib(n) { if (n < 2) return n; return fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1); } print fib(24); var xs = []; for (var i = 0; i < 20000; i = i + 1) { push(xs, str(i)); if (len(xs) > 100) xs = []; } print len(xs); var sum = 0; for (var i = 0; i < 200000; i = i + 1) sum = sum + i % 7; print sum;
notes: Tier A (M9 item 11.32): an Mk-only row, the lox dogfood unchanged, compared across mk binaries; no twin (a twin is a whole interpreter), no defect line (README.md).

The program is Dogfoods/lox/cases/scripts/bench.lox on one line through --eval, the script having no size argument: the quick arguments keep its counts (fib(24), 20,000 pushes, 200,000 sums) and print its bench.out; the publish arguments raise them (fib(26), 60,000 and 600,000).
The size is provisional; tools/bench verify -publish-size fixes it in the quiet window, and the checksum changes with it.
